Section One: District Council meetings

articles.heading: Councillors’ seats during the session (1) Councillors are given seats in accordance with the alphabetical order of their
articles.text:
surnames.
(2) The Minister in charge of local
government, any other Minister, State
Minister, other Cabinet member or a
member of Parliament who participates in
the District Council meeting is allocated a
special seat in the meeting room.

articles.heading: Quorum for the meeting of the District Council (1) The quorum for the meeting of the District
articles.text:
Council is two-thirds of its members.
22
However, when the meeting is convened
for the second time, it takes place
regardless of the number of its councillors
who are present in the meeting.
(2) A Councillor may not be represented at
District Council meetings.

articles.heading: Signing on the attendance list of the meeting Councillors sign on the attendance list of the
articles.text:
meeting. Before the meeting starts, the
Chairperson of the District Council meeting
announces the number of Councillors present
to ensure that the quorum required by the Law
has been obtained.

articles.heading: Agenda of the meeting of the District Council (1) The agenda of the meeting of the District
articles.text:
Council is prepared by its Bureau.
(2) Each Councillor has the right to propose an
item to be included on the agenda at least
one day before the meeting.
23

articles.heading: Amendment of the agenda of the meeting Items on the agenda of the District Council meeting may be amended before
articles.text:
commencement of the meeting if requested–
(a) by at least a third of Councillors who
are presents in the meeting; or
(b) by the Bureau of the District Council.

articles.heading: Taking the floor at the District Council meeting (1) A Councillor who intends to take the floor
articles.text:
in the District Council meeting seeks
permission from the Chairperson of the
meeting. The Chairperson authorises
interventions in accordance to the point of
request.
(2) The Minister in charge of local
government, any other Minister, State
Minister, other Cabinet member or a
member of Parliament who participates in
the District Council meeting, or
Councillors whose issues are being
debated, are allowed to intervene only
where they so request.
24

articles.heading: Councillor who is given floor whose name does not appear on the list of discussants (1) A Councillor whose name does not appear
articles.text:
on the list of discussants may be given the
floor only once and does not take more
than one minute for an item to–
(a) remind existing laws;
(b) comment on issues raised against
him or her;
(c) remind that the matter he or she
raised was not responded to;
(d) request that debates be suspended;
or
(e) submit for the adjournment of the
meeting.
(2) The submissions provided for in Paragraph
(1) (d) and (e) of this Article are approved
by a two-thirds majority of votes of the
Councillors who are present in the meeting.
Councillors who had raised issues are
responded to before closure of the debates
on the item under consideration or District
Council meeting closure.
25

articles.heading: Speakers’ position and the addressee (1) A person who is given the floor to speak stays in his or her seat unless it is directed
articles.text:
otherwise.
(2) A person who takes the floor addresses his
or her speech to the Chairperson of the
meeting or the District Council in general.

articles.heading: Discussions in the District Council meeting (1) The Chairperson of the District Council meeting announces the course of District
articles.text:
Council deliberations and concludes the
debates when all who have requested for
the floor have spoken.
(2) The Chairperson of the District Council
meeting or any Councillor may suggest
that the meeting stop if he or she believes
that the District Council has sufficiently
covered all the items on the agenda and
such a suggestion is approved by the
Council.
26

articles.heading: Council’s decision-making process (1) Decisions of the meeting of the District Council are taken by absolute majority
articles.text:
votes of members present. In the event of a
tie, voting is repeated. Where a tie persists,
the voting is postponed to another day until
the majority is obtained.
(2) The resolutions of the District Council are
implemented by the concerned
management organs.

articles.heading: Minutes of the meeting of the District Council (1) The District Council meeting is subject to
articles.text:
minutes which are adopted in the
subsequent meeting.
(2) The minutes of the District Council
meeting are signed by the Chairperson of
the meeting and the rapporteur.

articles.heading: Submission of the minutes of the District Council meeting (1) After approval of the minutes of the
articles.text:
District Council meeting, the Chairperson
of the District Council submits the minutes
27
to the Governor of the Province.
(2) The President of the District Council
submits the minutes to the Governor of the
Province within five working days from
the date of their approval and with
acknowledgment of receipt, and reserves a
copy to the executive authority of the
concerned organ.
(3) The authority to whom the minutes are
submitted may provide written comments
within five working days from the date of
their receipt, and reserves a copy to the
executive authority of the concerned organ.

articles.heading: Rights of members of Parliament to provide opinions in meetings of the District Council Members of Parliament are authorized to
articles.text:
attend meetings of the District Council and
give their views without having the right to
vote.

articles.heading: Rights of Cabinet members to attend the District Council meeting (1) The Minister in charge of local government
articles.text:
may attend or send a representative
28
authorized by a written proxy to attend
meetings of the District Council when
there is an item on the agenda on which he
or she wants to provide an opinion, but he
or she has no right to vote.
(2) Other Cabinet members are allowed to
attend or send a representatives authorized
by a written proxy to attend meetings of the
District Council to provide an opinion if
the agenda includes an item relevant to
their responsibilities, but they have no right
to vote.

articles.heading: Other persons who may be invited to the District Council meeting The District Council may invite any other
articles.text:
person to attend its meeting. However, the
invitee has no right to vote.

articles.heading: Postponement of the District Council meeting In case there is a compelling reason to postpone a scheduled meeting, the Chairperson
articles.text:
of the District Council informs the Councillors
29
in advance by use of the fastest and appropriate
means of communication with
acknowledgement of receipt.

articles.heading: Public sessions Meetings of the District Council are open to the public. Particularly, the District Council
articles.text:
must meet in public where items like the
budget, matters related to taxes, loans or funds
held in a bank account and use of property are
on the items proposed on the agenda.

articles.heading: District Council meetings in closed session (1) The District Council meeting may be held in closed session upon request by twothirds of members present or in c
articles.text:
consideration of matters regarding
individuals.
(2) When it is decided that the District Council
holds a close session meeting such a
decision is notified to the public through
quickest possible means facilitating its fast
dissemination.
(3) When the District Council is in meeting
and is required to discuss matters involving
30
an individual, the Chairperson of the
meeting immediately orders that the
meeting be held in closed session and it can
be reopened to the public if the debates in
closed session are over.

articles.heading: Declaration of interest (1) When a Councillor has a direct or indirect interest in the issue under consideration by
articles.text:
the Council, the concerned Councillor
notifies the Council. In that case, the
Councillor is excluded during
consideration of the issue.
(2) When the matter to be examined regards
the Chairperson of the meeting, he or she is
replaced in accordance with relevant laws.

articles.heading: Powers to establish instructions The District Council has powers to establish instructions to be enforced within its territorial
articles.text: limits.

articles.heading: Conformity with laws and general regulations (1) Instructions and resolutions of the District
articles.text:
31
Council must be in conformity with laws
and general regulations.
(2) A decision taken by the District Council
which was irregularly held or contrary to
the Law, is invalid.

articles.heading: Security of meetings of the District Council (1) The Chairperson of the meeting ensures the
articles.text:
security of the District Council meeting.
He or she may give a warning to a person
who causes disturbance at the meeting and
may expel him or her from that meeting if
he or she fails to follow the given warning.
(2) If the Chairperson of the meeting expels a
person, he or she makes a written statement
on the expulsion which is approved by that
meeting, and may refer him or her to
relevant organs where necessary.
Section 2: Procedures used in submitting
issues and taking decisions
32

articles.heading: Submission of an issue to be examined in the District Council meeting (1) A Councillor has the right to submit an
articles.text:
issue in writing to the Chairperson of the
District Council for consideration.
(2) An issue to be examined in the District
Council meeting is accompanied by its
explanatory note. The Bureau of the
District Council submits the issue together
with its explanatory note to each
Councillor within seven working days
from the date the issue was submitted to the
Bureau of the Council.

articles.heading: Debates on the issue submitted (1) The Chairperson of the District Council presents to the District Council an issue
articles.text:
submitted to the Bureau of the District
Council for discussion.
(2) Discussions are carried out in presence of
the petitioner who provides details on the
issue and responds to questions related to
the basis of the subject.
33
(3) The District Council decides on the issue
or decides whether it is forwarded to the
relevant Commission for detailed
examination.
(4) A Councillor who has an opinion on the
issue forwarded to a Commission, submits
it in writing to the Chairperson of the
concerned Commission and reserves a
copy to all Councillors.

articles.heading: Commission that examines an issue (1) If a Commission declares itself incompetent for the examination of an
articles.text:
issue or when the issue concerns several
Commissions, the Bureau of the District
Council decides which Commission must
examine it.
(2) The Commission, after consideration of the
issue submitted to it, prepares a report and
submits it to the Bureau of the Council.
(3) An issue whose provisions or parts require
revision is referred back to the
Commission for perfection.
34
(4) The report on revision of provisions or
parts of provisions referred back to the
Commission is forwarded to the Bureau of
the District Council at least two working
days before it is considered by the Council.

articles.heading: Invitation of an employee to the Commission A Commission through a member of District Executive Committee responsible for the item
articles.text:
to be discussed, may invite the concern
employee to provide explanations to the
Commission that examines an issue he or she
is responsible.

articles.heading: Modalities of adoption of the resolutions (1) The District Council takes resolutions through voting
articles.text:
(2) Before voting, the Chairperson of the
District Council announces the number of
Councillors present basing on those who
signed on the attendance list or using
electronic system.
(3) The vote is taken by –
35
(a) consensus;
(b) show of hand;
(c) electronic means
(d) secret ballot; or
(e) roll call.

articles.heading: Consensus, show of hand and electronic means Consensus, show of hand and electronic means are the voting modalities used by the District
articles.text:
Council during the discussions of other issues
except for instructions.

articles.heading: Secret ballot Secret ballot is used when requested by at least two-thirds of Councillors present in the
articles.text:
meeting or when the District Council takes
decisions regarding individuals.

articles.heading: Roll call When using roll call in voting, the individual 36 called replies “yes”, “no” or “abstention” in a
articles.text: clear voice.

articles.heading: Adopting resolutions on instructions, a proposal or an issue (1) Adoption of each Article of instructions is
articles.text:
done by show of hand or electronic means.
(2) After voting each article of the instructions,
the vote of the entire bill of instructions
follows and the roll call is used.
(3) If, after counting votes, an item does not
obtain the required number of votes, a
Councillor or the Commission which
considered the draft instructions or their
representative, through the Chairperson of
the Council, may request that the article be
referred back to the Commission upon
approval by the District Council by
absolute majority votes. If there is no such
request, that article is dropped.
(4) If it is an issue or a proposal that was voted and
does not obtain the required majority, it is
returned to the person who presented it.
37
(5) If there is no absolute majority vote during
the vote of draft instructions, the Bureau of
the District Council returns the draft to the
District Council after 15 working days for
re-voting.

articles.heading: Adoption of a resolution by roll call (1) The Chairperson of the Council, during voting, requests the Secretary of the
articles.text:
District Council to call each individual by
name in accordance with the alphabetical
order of surnames of the individuals.
(2) A vote of a Councillor who does not show
his or her position in elections but who is
present in the meeting or who signed an
attendance list but who is absent during
voting is regarded as invalid.

articles.heading: Adoption of a resolution by secret ballot (1) If the vote is conducted through secret ballot, the Secretary of the District Council
articles.text:
gives each Councillor present, a ballot
38
paper prepared for that purpose by the
Chairperson of the meeting.
(2) If the Secretary is absent, his or her duties
in the District Council meetings are carried
out by the Deputy Chairperson of the
Council.
(3) After voting, each Councillor places the
ballot paper in the ballot box provided for
that purpose. The used ballot papers are
then sorted in front of the Councillors by a
representative of the Bureau assisted by
two Councillors, led by the Chairperson of
the Council.
(4) Unused ballots papers and those different
from ballot papers prepared by the
Chairperson of the meeting are invalid.

articles.heading: Value of vote and interdiction of proxy voting (1) Regardless of the voting method used, each
articles.text:
Councillor has only one vote.
(2) Voting by proxy is not accepted.

articles.heading: Counting of votes (1) The counting of votes is done by two 39 Councillors nominated by the Bureau of
articles.text:
the District Council and assisted by an
employee designated by the Chairperson of
the Council.
(2) After counting the votes, the Chairperson
of the District Council announces to the
District Council the results from the vote.

articles.heading: Giving reasons for abstention After each vote, whether by consensus, show of hand, roll call or electronic means, the
articles.text:
Chairperson of the District Council allows
Councillors who abstained, if they so request,
to give reasons why they did so in a period not
exceeding two minutes. These reasons are not
debatable.

articles.heading: Destruction of used ballot papers If the vote was conducted through secret ballot, the used ballot papers are destroyed in front of
articles.text:
the District Council after the vote.
40

articles.heading: Prohibition to take floor during voting 12
Right of access to the resolutions of the District Council (1) A very citizen has the right to access the
articles.text:
resolutions of the Council. He or she has
the right to access the minutes of the
District Council meeting and read them
from the office where they are kept.
(2) The resolutions of the District Council
meeting are communicated to the public in
accordance with the legal provisions
governing the publication of administrative
acts.
(3) However, the District Council may decide
that its decisions made in closed session be
kept secret until when it deems no longer
necessary to keep them as such.
41

articles.heading: Requesting the District Council to revoke its decision (1) Interested person may petition the District
articles.text:
Council to revoke its decision within a
period not exceeding 30 days from its
publication as provided by Law, indicating
the provisions which have been violated.
(2) If the District Council does not respond
within 60 days following the petition to
reconsider its resolution, the petitioner may
request the competent organ to decide upon
the resolution.
CHAPTER II: COUNCILLORS’
CONDUCT AND INVIOLABILITY OF
COUNCIL
Section One: Councillors’ conduct in
District Council meetings

articles.heading: Conduct of the Chairperson of the meeting during debates (1) The Chairperson of the District Council
articles.text:
meeting is independent and impartial
42
during debates.
(2) The Chairperson of the District Council
meeting resists coercive action during
debates and in the process of decisionmaking.

articles.heading: Conduct during the District Council meeting (1) A person must not interrupt a speaker except the Chairperson of the meeting who
articles.text:
only does so when reminding the speaker
about laws, orders or regulations governing
the functioning of the Council.
(2) If the speaker strays from the subject of
discussion or repeats what has already been
said, the Chairperson of the meeting has
the power to interrupt him or her and to
remind the speaker of the subject under
consideration.
(3) If, after a second reminder, the speaker
continues to deviate from the subject of
discussion or repeat what has already been
said, the Chairperson of the meeting cuts
him or her off for the duration of the
Council’s debate on that subject.
43
(4) A Councillor may not be prosecuted for
opinions expressed during District Council
meetings, except in cases punishable by
law.

articles.heading: Prohibitions in the District Council meeting Any offensive language, any provocation, any intervention disrupting order or any act aimed
articles.text:
at preventing a speaker from expressing
himself or herself during District Council
meetings are prohibited.

articles.heading: Order in the meeting (1) A Councillor must be orderly in the meeting. The Chairperson of the meeting
articles.text:
calls by name any Councillor who disrupts
District Council meeting reminding him or
her to be orderly.
(2) If the Councillor who disrupts District
Council meetings repeats, the Chairperson
of the meeting cautions him or her and it is
recorded in the minutes of the meeting.
(3) If the Councillor persists in disrupting the
meeting or in case any other serious reason
arises, the Chairperson of the meeting,
44
upon approval of two-thirds of the votes of
the Councillors present, pronounces
temporary exclusion of the Councillor
from the seats of Councillors.

articles.heading: Effect of temporary exclusion from the Councillors’ seats Temporary exclusion of a Councillor who
articles.text:
disrupts a District Council meeting
automatically denies him or her the right to
participate in the District Council proceedings
and in decision-making along with other
Councillors during the remaining period of the
meeting in which he or she has been excluded.

articles.heading: Refusal by a Councillor to vacate his or her seat or to comply with measures of exclusion and its effect
articles.text:
When a Councillor who is temporarily
excluded due to reasons referred to in Articles
48 and 49 of these Rules of procedure refuses
to comply with the order to vacate his or her
seat, the Chairperson of the meeting suspends
the meeting deliberations for a while or for the
remainder of the meeting. In that case, the
Councillor is excluded for the next three
consecutive District Council meetings,
45
reprimanded in writing and suspended from
three consecutive meetings of the
Commission.

articles.heading: End of exclusion of Councillor (1) A Councillor’s exclusion order from meetings, is lifted –
articles.text:
(a) if the excluded Councillor makes
an apology to the District Council
and the latter concedes;
(b) if the District Council retracts its
decision upon proposal by the
Bureau; or
(c) if the exclusion period expires.
(2) If the excluded Councillor apologizes in
writing, the Chairperson of the District
Council reads his or her apology before the
Councillors in the District Council
meeting, and take a decision.
46

articles.heading: Suspension of the meeting when there is commotion When there is commotion during the District
articles.text:
Council meeting, the Chairperson of the
meeting intervenes and calls for order. When it
continues, the Chairperson suspends the
meeting and Councillors leave the meeting
room. The meeting resumes when the
Chairperson is convinced that sufficient order
has been restored.
Section 2: District Council inviolability

articles.heading: Sitting in seats reserved for Councillors No person, other than a Councillor, sits in seats
articles.text: reserved for Councillors.

articles.heading: Public seats and order in the District Council meeting room (1) Members of the public attending the
articles.text:
business of the District Council meeting
take seats reserved for them, remain silent,
and remove their hats except those who are
authorized to wear hats due to their
occupation, religion, or by permission of
47
the Council. When the District Council
decides to sit in a closed session, the public
leaves the meeting room.
(2) A person who enters a District Council
meeting room with a mobile telephone or
any other electronic equipment or device
that may interfere with the proper conduct
of the District Council meeting switches it
off or puts it in silent mode.

articles.heading: Expulsion of a person who disrupts the District Council meeting The Chairperson of the District Council
articles.text:
meeting may instruct the responsible persons
to immediately expel from the meeting room
any member of the public who disrupts the
District Council session.

articles.heading: Communication of provisions related to District Council inviolability Provisions of these rules of procedure that are
articles.text:
related to the District Council inviolability are
communicated to the public which attends the
District Council meeting.
48
CHAPTER III: FUNCTIONING OF THE
BUREAU OF THE COUNCIL

articles.heading: Members of the Bureau of the District Council The District Council is chaired by a Bureau composed of three members, namely the
articles.text:
Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson and the
Secretary.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Chairperson of the District Council The Chairperson of the District Council has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to chair and coordinate activities of the
Bureau and those of the Council;
(b) to convene and chair meetings of the
Council;
(c) to convene and chair the meeting that
brings together the Bureau of the
District Council and Chairpersons of
Councils of the Sectors that make up
the District, at least twice a year;
(d) to perform any other duty related to his
49
or her responsibilities as may be
assigned by the Council.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Deputy Chairperson of the District Council The Deputy Chairperson of the District
articles.text:
Council deputizes the Chairperson and
replaces him or her in case of absence.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Secretary of the District Council The Secretary of the District Council has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to be the rapporteur of the District
Council;
(b) to prepare quarterly action plan and
summary report indicating the District
Council activities;
(c) to prepare a summary report that
contains decisions of the District
Council and to submit them to
Councillors for approval;
(d) to draw up a list of Councillors wishing
50
to take the floor;
(e) to receive, dispatch and file documents
of the District Council;
(f) to perform any other duty falling within
the responsibilities of the District
Council as may be assigned by the
Council.

articles.heading: Decisions of the Bureau of the District Council The decisions of the Bureau of the District
articles.text:
Council are taken by consensus. In case the
consensus is not reached, the issue is submitted
to a vote and the decision is taken by an
absolute majority of the votes of the members.

articles.heading: Loss of membership of the Bureau (1) A member of the Bureau of the District Council loses membership upon
articles.text:
resignation or due to any reason preventing
him or her from being among members of
the Bureau of the Council.
(2) When the Chairperson of the District
Council resigns, he or she addresses the
resignation letter to the District Council
51
members with a copy to the authority of the
administrative entity which supervises the
District Council.
(3) In case the resignation is from the Vice
Chairperson or the Secretary of the District
Council or both, the resigning person
individually addresses the resignation
letter to the Chairperson of the Council,
with a copy to the authority of the
administrative entity which supervises the
District Council.
(4) In case of resignation of the entire Bureau,
each resigning member addresses his or her
resignation letter to the Councillors, with a
copy to the executive authority of the
immediate superior organ to the one to
which he or she is a Councillor.
(5) The District Council confirms the
cessation of duties of a member of the
Bureau through an absolute majority of the
votes of the Councillors meeting in an
extraordinary session.

articles.heading: Temporary replacement of the Chairperson of the District Council In case the Chairperson of the District Council
articles.text:
ceases his or her duties, the Vice-Chairperson
52
assumes the office pending elections for his or
her replacement.

articles.heading: Convening and chairing an extraordinary meeting to confirm the cessation of duties of the Chairperson of the
articles.text:
District Council or all members of the
Bureau
(1) Where the cessation of duties concerns the
Chairperson of the Council, the Deputy
Chairperson convenes and chairs the
extraordinary session referred to in Article
63(5) of these rules of procedure.
(2) The Deputy Chairperson, upon his or her
own initiative or upon request by at least a
third of Councillors, convenes an
extraordinary meeting within a period not
exceeding five working days from the date
of receipt of the request to convene the
meeting or the date of request of cessation
of duties of Chairperson of the Council.
(3) When the cessation of duties concerns all
members of the Bureau, the oldest
Councillor among the Councillors with the
most seniority in the District Council
convenes and chairs, within the period
provided for in Paragraph (2) of this
53
Article, the extraordinary session referred
to in Article 63(5) of these rules of
procedure.

articles.heading: Election to replace members of the Bureau who ceased to hold office (1) The District Council meeting for the
articles.text:
purpose of electing a member or members
of the Bureau replacing those who have
ceased to hold office is convened by the
Governor of the Province, within a period
not exceeding 60 days from the date the
District Council confirmed their permanent
cessation of duties.
(2) The person elected to replace a member
who has vacated his or her office from the
Bureau completes the term of office of his
or her predecessor.

articles.heading: Consideration of a personal issue concerning the Chairperson If the District Council is considering an issue
articles.text:
concerning the Chairperson of the Council, or
if he or she wants to give his or her personal
opinion, the Deputy Chairperson chairs the
54
meeting. In case the Deputy Chairperson is
absent, the District Council members choose
its Chairperson from among themselves.
During that period, the Chairperson of the
District Council sits in the seat reserved for
him or her as a Councillor.
CHAPTER IV: DISTRICT COUNCIL
COMMISSIONS
Section One: Standing Commissions

articles.heading: Standing Commissions of the Council (1) The District Council consists of the following Commissions
articles.text:
(a) Commission of Finance and
Economic Development;
(b) Commission for promotion of
Social Welfare;
(c) Commission of Good Governance.
(2) Each Councillor is a member of one of the
Commissions. Members of each
Commission are determined by the Bureau
55
of the District Council and each
Commission is made up of at least five
Councillors.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Commission on Finance and Economic Development The Commission on Finance and Economic
articles.text:
Development has the following
responsibilities:
(a) to follow up the implementation of the
decisions of the District Council in
finance and economic development
matters;
(b) to follow up development projects;
(c) to develop strategies meant to increase
assets;
(d) to sensitize the population on
development activities;
(e) to sensitize the population to work in
cooperatives;
(f) to develop draft directives to be
considered by the District Council in
line with the responsibilities of the
56
Commission;
(g) to consider such other issues falling
within its responsibilities as may be
assigned by the Council.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Commission for promotion of Social Welfare The Commission for promotion of Social
articles.text:
Welfare has the following responsibilities:
(a) to follow up the implementation of the
decisions of the District Council in
matters related to the promotion of
social welfare;
(b) to follow up the implementation of
strategies related to the promotion of
women, youth, people with disabilities,
the protection of children’s rights, and
the promotion of culture and sports;
(c) to develop strategies for the
implementation of policies meant to
support and protect vulnerable people;
(d) to carry out analysis and provide advice
on harmonization of public and private
57
initiatives in matters related to social
welfare;
(e) to develop a program designed to
support the implementation of the
policies on health, education, hygiene
and sanitation;
(f) to develop drafts of directives to be
considered by the District Council in
line with the responsibilities of the
Commission;
(g) to develop a viable program designed
to teach illiterate population;
(h) to consider such other issues falling
within its responsibilities as may be
assigned by the Council.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the Commission of Good Governance The Commission of Good Governance has the
articles.text:
following responsibilities:
(a) to follow up the implementation of the
decisions of the District Council as
regards administrative, political and
legal affairs;
58
(b) to develop strategies on the safety of
persons and property;
(c) to develop drafts of directives to be
considered by the District Council in
connection with the responsibilities of
the Commission;
(d) to settle issues related to governance,
laws and policies;
(e) to monitor the management of civil
registration and registration of the
population;
(f) to consider such other issues falling
within its responsibilities as may be
assigned by the Council.

articles.heading: Duty of the Commission in relation to consideration of public petitions Each Commission is responsible for receiving
articles.text:
and examining the petitions submitted to the
District Council by the population, in relation
to the responsibilities assigned to the
Commission.
59

articles.heading: Appointment of members of standing Commissions Members of standing Commissions of the District Council are appointed according to the
articles.text:
following steps:
(a) each Councillor registers in one
Commission;
(b) the Bureau of the District Council
verifies the registration of Councillors
and confirms the composition of each
Commission in consideration of the
following criteria:
(i) the desire of each Councillor to
register in a Commission;
(ii) the number of members of each
Commission;
(iii) the mandate of the standing
Commission;
(iv) the expertise and skills of a
Councillor in relation to the
standing Commission’s
responsibilities;
(v) the principle of gender equality.
60

articles.heading: Structure of the Commission (1) Each Commission is chaired by a Bureau, composed of a Chairperson and a
articles.text:
Rapporteur who are elected by the District
Council by absolute majority vote of
Councillors present.
(2) To be elected, members of each
Commission who want to stand as
candidates inform the Bureau of the
District Council of their intention, which in
turn informs the Council.
(3) The Chairperson and Rapporteur of the
Commission are elected each separately. If,
after voting, no candidate obtains the
required majority, the vote is repeated.
(4) When the absolute majority is not obtained
for the second round, the candidate with
the highest number of votes is elected.
(5) When the Chairperson and the Rapporteur,
for any reason, are prevented from chairing
the Commission or when they have
permanently left their posts and they have
61
not yet been replaced, the Commission is
chaired by the eldest Councillor among the
members of the Commission present. The
youngest Councillor serves as the
Rapporteur.

articles.heading: Replacement of members of the Bureau of a Commission (1) The Bureau of a Commission or one of its
articles.text:
members may be replaced upon
resignation or upon request of one-third of
the members of the Commission. The letter
of resignation or request for replacement is
addressed to the Chairperson of the
Council.
(2) The replacement referred to in Paragraph
(1) of this Article is done within a period of
30 days in accordance with the provisions
relating to election of the Bureau of the
Commission.

articles.heading: Frequency of meetings of the Commission The Commission meeting convenes once a month in an ordinary session and whenever
articles.text:
necessary.
62

articles.heading: Councillors eligible to attend activities of the Commission (1) Each Councillor is allowed to attend
articles.text:
activities of any Commission even if he or
she is not a member of that Commission.
(2) A Councillor who attends activities of a
Commission of which he or she is not a
member does not receive any sitting or
transport allowances unless he or she is
invited in writing by the Commission to
provide opinion or clarifications to the item
on the agenda.

articles.heading: Agenda of the meeting of the Commission The Chairperson of the Commission and the Rapporteur prepare the agenda of the meeting
articles.text:
of the Commission and inform the Chairperson
of the District Council and the Mayor of
District.

articles.heading: Venue of the meetings (1) The meetings of the Commission are held at the head office of the District
articles.text:
(2) When necessary, and after the Bureau of
the Commission has made consultations
63
with the Bureau of the Council, the
Commission may convene in a place other
than the District head office but in the
territory of the same District.

articles.heading: Quorum of the meeting of the Commission The quorum for the meeting of the Commission is at least two-thirds of its
articles.text: members.

articles.heading: Decision-making in the Commission Decisions of the Commission are taken by absolute majority votes of the Councillors
articles.text: present.

articles.heading: Official mission The Bureau of the Commission or all members of the Commission may go on official mission
articles.text:
or conduct study tours to other institutions with
a notification to the District Council Bureau
and the Executive Secretary of the District.
64

articles.heading: Report of the Commission The Commission submits its report to the District Council on activity accomplished. The
articles.text:
report consists of a summary of discussions
and resolutions adopted.

articles.heading: Submission of proposal to the Commission Every Councillor has the right to submit to the Commission, in writing, his or her opinion on
articles.text: any item on the Commission’s agenda.

articles.heading: Preparation of draft or submission of a petition (1) A Councillor who prepares a draft, who
articles.text:
intends to submit a petition, an opinion or
an amendment attends the Commission
meetings convened for that purpose. The
Councillor is not allowed to vote unless he
or she is a member of that Commission.
(2) An amendment to regulations, proposal or
petition is submitted in writing to the
relevant Commission for consideration and
resolution to be submitted to the Council.
65
Section 2: Ad hoc Commissions

articles.heading: Establishment of an ad hoc Commission On request by the Chairperson of the District Council and upon approval by the District
articles.text:
Council meeting, the District Council may
establish an ad hoc Commission to examine
arising exceptional issues.

articles.heading: Appointment of members of an ad hoc Commission The Bureau of the District Council submits a
articles.text:
list of proposed candidates for the ad hoc
Commission to the District Council for
approval. The District Council also appoints
the Chairperson and the Rapporteur of the
Commission from a list of two candidates
proposed by the Bureau on each post.

articles.heading: Duration of ad hoc Commission duties and their conclusion (1) The District Council determines the
articles.text:
duration and duties of the ad hoc
Commission.
66
(2) The ad hoc Commission ends its duties
after it has submitted a report of
achievements and after the District Council
has taken decision on it.

articles.heading: Allowances of members of the ad hoc Commission The District Council determines allowances to
articles.text:
be paid to members of the ad hoc Commission
when they participate in the works of the
Commission.
CHAPTER V: EXTENDED BUREAU OF
THE DISTRICT COUNCIL

articles.heading: Members of the extended Bureau of the Council The extended Bureau of the District Council is
articles.text:
composed of members of the Bureau of the
District Council and chairpersons of the
standing Commissions.

articles.heading: Responsibilities of the extended Bureau of the Council The extended Bureau of the District Council
articles.text:
has the following responsibilities:
(a) to approve minutes of the meetings of
67
the Commissions to be submitted to the
Council;
(b) to submit to the Council, within a
period of 30 days, urgent resolutions
taken for approval;
(c) to consider issues related to
Councillors, the District Council itself
and Commissions, and submit them to
the District Council for decision.

articles.heading: Functioning of the extended Bureau of the Council (1) The extended Bureau of the District Council holds a meeting once a quarter and
articles.text:
whenever necessary.
(2) The meeting of the extended Bureau of the
District Council is convened and chaired
by the Chairperson of the Council. The
Secretary to the Bureau of the District
Council is the rapporteur of the extended
Bureau of the Council.
(3) The extended Bureau of the District
Council submits a written report on its
activities to the District Council before the
68
District Council convenes.
(4) The extended Bureau of the District
Council may invite to its meeting the
members of the Executive Committee or
any other District authority.
CHAPTER VI: FUNCTIONNING OF THE
EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE

articles.heading: Frequency of meetings of the Executive Committee The Executive Committee meets at least once
articles.text:
a week and whenever necessary to draw up
strategies for carrying out its responsibilities.

articles.heading: Decision-making process Decisions of the Executive Committee are taken by consensus. In case the consensus is
articles.text:
not reached, the issue is submitted to the next
scheduled District Council meeting for
decision.

articles.heading: Prohibitions to members of the Executive Committee A member of the Executive Committee is prohibited from –
articles.text:
69
(a) participating in a District Council
meeting that examines matters in
which he or she has direct or indirect
interest;
(b) directly or indirectly taking part in
business activities in which the District
is involved;
(c) collecting taxes and duties; and
(d) being personally engaged in business
activities.

articles.heading: Leave of members of the Executive Committee Members of the Executive Committee cannot take their annual leave simultaneously. The
articles.text:
District Council approves the period of leave
for a member of the Executive Committee.
CHAPTER VII: MISCELLANEOUS
PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Budget of the District Council The District allocates in its annual budget, the budget reserved for the District Council to
articles.text:
70
enable it to discharge its responsibilities.

articles.heading: Allowances granted to a Councillor sent on official mission (1) A member of the Bureau of the District
articles.text:
Council on official mission is entitled to
allowances equivalent to those given to the
District Mayor on official mission.
(2) A Councillor of the District on official
mission is entitled to allowances
equivalent to those given to the ViceMayor on official mission.

articles.heading: Dismissal of a Councillor who fails to discharge his or her duties A Councillor who fails to discharge his or her
articles.text:
duties is dismissed in the following manner:
(a) the Chairperson of the District Council
makes a detailed report on the
Councillor’s inability to perform his or
her duties, and informs other
Councillors and the Councillor
concerned, requesting him or her to
provide written explanations within 30
71
days from the day of notification;
(b) the Chairperson of the District Council
refers the matter to the District Council
for decision after considering the report
together with the explanations
provided by the concerned Councillor;
(c) if the explanations are not accepted, the
District Council requests the
Councillor concerned to resign;
(d) when the Councillor refuses to resign,
he or she is dismissed by the District
Council upon approval by at least twothirds of Councillors.

articles.heading: Replacement of a Councillor (1) When a Councillor resigns, is dismissed by the District Council or has any reason that
articles.text:
prevents him or her from continuing to
discharge his or her duties, an election is
held to replace him or her within 60 days
from his or her ceasing of duties.
72
(2) However, when the remaining term of
office is not more than six months, no other
Councillor is elected.
CHAPTER VIII: FINAL PROVISIONS

articles.heading: Iterana ry’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere (1) Inama Njyanama y’Akarere iterana rimwe mu mezi atatu mu nama isanzwe,
articles.text:
ikabera ku biro by’Akarere cyangwa
ahandi mu ifasi yako byemejwe na Biro
y’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere.
(2) Icyakora, Inama Njyanama y’Akarere
iterana mu nama idasanzwe igihe cyose
bibaye ngombwa cyangwa bisabwe mu
nyandiko nibura na kimwe cya gatatu
cy’abayigize. Inama idasanzwe yiga gusa
ibiri ku murongo w’ibyigwa.

articles.heading: Kwitabira inama z’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere Kwitabira inama z’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere ni itegeko kuri buri mujyanama keretse iyo hari
articles.text:
impamvu igaragara imubuza kuyitabira. Ubusabe
bwo kutitabira inama bushyikirizwa Perezida
w’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere mu nyandiko
nibura umunsi umwe mbere y’uko iterana.

articles.heading: Kumenyesha iterana ry’inama z’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere Inama Njyanama y’Akarere igena amatariki
articles.text:
y’inama z’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere kandi
inama zikamenyeshwa Guverineri w’Intara
n’undi muyobozi w’urwego bireba bitewe
n’ingingo ziri ku murongo w’ibyigwa.

articles.heading: Kwitabira kwa Perezida na Visi Perezida Perezida na Visi Perezida b’Inama Njyanama y’Akarere ntibashobora kugira rimwe mu
articles.text:
mirimo ibabuza kuyobora Inama Njyanama
y’Akarere igihe inama yayo yatumijwe.

articles.heading: Gutangira gukurikizwa ITEKA RYA MINISITIRI N° 007/07.01 RYO KU WA 13/07/2023 RYEREKEYE AMATEGEKO NGENGAMIKORERE
articles.text:
